messages:
beth: Customer on enterprise tier reports analytics CSV export returns a 0-byte file when the segmentation includes a null bucket (e.g. plan: null) and the date range > 60 days. They attached curl output and say it used to work last month. can someone triage?
support-bot: Ticket #C-8241 created, linked to customer account acme-inc. Uploads: presigned-s3. Priority: P2.
maya: :eyes: can you paste the exact export request and the headers you saw? UI or API?
beth: API request they used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"dataset":"user_activity","format":"csv","filters":{"plan":null,"country":"US"},"range":{"start":"2024-10-01","end":"2025-01-31"}}'
```
Response headers from their client: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Type: text/csv`, `Content-Length: 0`
beth: They also showed the presigned PUT to S3 returned 200 but object size is 0 in bucket.
liam: any chance the exporter is gzipping body but not setting Content-Encoding? we've had that mismatch before. can you grab the export job id?
beth: job id: export_20250115_2789 (from admin console). I pulled our export service logs for that id: `export_worker: start job export_20250115_2789, query: SELECT ... WHERE (plan = 'null' OR plan IS NULL) AND ts BETWEEN ...`
liam: hmm that query looks suspect — why is plan = 'null' showing up? looks like frontend translates the UI null selection into string 'null' for some customers. If query returns no rows, the stream should still emit headers. 0-byte indicates the streaming writer closed before header was written.
engbot: recent commit d3f9a8 (export-stream): changed stream flush to be deferred until first row to avoid writing single-row headers for tiny exports. regressions reported when rowcount==0.
maya: ok assigning to @liam (backend) and @maya for triage. quick repro steps for local: 1) create test dataset with a null plan row 2) run same export API with filter plan=null and date range > 60d 3) inspect presigned PUT size
liam: tried repro locally with fixture: got same behavior — S3 object 0 bytes, exporter logs show stream ended without writing header. temporary workaround: remove null filter or use the dataset API to export JSON (json export works and includes empty array).
beth: customer can't use JSON (they rely on CSV ingestion). they've asked for ETA. they're hitting downstream ETL jobs failing because file is empty.
liam: root cause: stream writer waits for first row to allocate a gzip/writer and to write header to avoid extra memory; for zero-row result the code path closed underlying HTTP writer before header. code fix: ensure header is written to the response before checking rowcount. I'll open a PR and add unit tests for zero-row exports + integration test against presigned-s3.
maya: please include a migration in the patch to re-run failed jobs for last 7 days for enterprise customers automatically (or at least a queued retry).
liam: created PR #3312, CI running. Plan: hotfix branch -> rollout to staging in 1h -> prod hotfix after smoke tests (target 4h).
sre-bot: Incident runbook: add temporary policy to block any export jobs with filter plan=null for ranges > 30d until patch is deployed.
beth: I applied the block and told customer the ETA ~4-6 hours and provided workaround (do export with date <= 30d or remove null filter). customer replied :thumbsup: and asked to be notified when patch is live.
maya: after PR merges we'll run backfill for affected enterprise exports from last 48 hours. logging task: liam to leave verbose export logs for 24h post-deploy.
liam: noted. I'll also add defensive parsing so frontend can't send the literal string 'null' — convert null filter to explicit SQL `IS NULL`.
maya: thanks team. next steps summarized: 1) liam hotfix PR + smoke -> prod 2) lift block and notify customer 3) run retries/backfill 4) add frontend validation to avoid 'null' string 5) add tests for zero-row CSV header.
beth: updated ticket and pinged the customer when we apply the patch. closing internal thread when prod deploy done. :white_check_mark:
